# Frettler

> Frettler is a document-based macOS application for exploring scales, modes, chords and fretboard theory across guitar, bass, ukulele, mandolin and banjo.

Frettler combines interactive fretboards, chord organisers and persistent document-based workspaces. It is designed for musicians, teachers and students who want to explore music theory, organise ideas and save reusable learning documents.

## Current features

- **Favourite chord voicings:** Save a preferred voicing for each chord, instrument and tuning. Available favourites become the initial voicing when a diagram is created, its chord is changed, or the document's instrument or tuning changes. Favourites are stored locally across documents.
- **Customisable keyboard bindings:** The Keyboard tab in Settings records replacement shortcuts and restores individual defaults. Changes apply across open documents and are saved on the Mac; conflicting Frettler assignments are reported.
- **Collapsible panels:** Collapse or expand fretboards and chord organisers using the title control, a title double-click or a keyboard shortcut. Collapsed states are saved with the document; header chips retain a summary of the contents.
- **Panel navigation:** Focus and reveal panels with keyboard shortcuts, jump to the first or last panel, and move panels up or down. Expanded chord organisers also support chord focus and reordering shortcuts.
- **Printing:** Print fretboards, marked groups, chord organisers and full panel notepad text using the macOS print dialogue, or save a PDF. Vector layouts support colour, portrait, landscape and scaling.
- **Chord inversions:** Slash-chord titles identify the bass note of inversions, with an information popover explaining them. Chords settings control whether inversions and voicings with omitted notes are included.
- **Marquee play and marking:** Drag over visible fretboard notes to strum them, or to mark/unmark them in marking mode. Drag direction controls playback order or marking versus unmarking. Replay remembers the last played selection, respects current note/string filters and supports reverse playback.

## Product

- [Frettler Home](https://frettler.app/): Product overview, features and App Store download.
- [Changelog](https://frettler.app/changelog.html): Release history, new features, improvements and fixes, with additional details and screenshots.
- [Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/id6757320106): Download Frettler for macOS.

## Documentation

- [Getting Started](https://frettler.app/help/getting-started.html): Creating documents, choosing instruments and adding panels.
- [Supported Instruments](https://frettler.app/help/instruments.html): Guitar, bass, ukulele, mandolin and banjo support.
- [Document Window Overview](https://frettler.app/help/document-window-overview.html): Documents, collapsible panels, keyboard navigation, panel reordering, play modes and printing.
- [Fretboard Panels](https://frettler.app/help/fretboard-panels-overview.html): Working with scales, modes, chords, marking groups, collapsible panels and fretboard controls.
- [Marquee Selections](https://frettler.app/help/marquee-selections.html): Directional marquee play, filtered replay and reverse replay, plus marking and unmarking visible notes.
- [Chord Organiser Panels](https://frettler.app/help/chord-organiser-overview.html): Building chord collections, favourite voicings, inversions, omitted-note warnings and chord navigation.
- [Settings](https://frettler.app/help/frettler-settings.html): General, Documents, Instruments, Fretboards, Chords, Keyboard and Support tabs, including customisable shortcuts and voicing preferences.

## Company

- [Efford Studio Limited](https://frettler.app/): Independent UK software studio developing Frettler.
